questions: When the board is fully in view, are there exactly three pens on it (no missing pen and no empty gap)?
Do all three pens point the same direction, with none flipped or reversed relative to the other two?
Are all three pens the same color as each other, with none differing in color?
Is every pen complete and capped, with none showing a bare/exposed writing tip or looking clearly shorter than the others?
Does the board move smoothly and continuously from left to right, without stopping, freezing, pausing, reversing, or jamming at any point?

question_answers.evidence: At 00:08-00:10, three distinct pen-shaped objects are visible on the white board.
The leftmost pen has a pointed tip facing down, while the middle and right pens have caps facing down. They are not oriented identically.
All three pens have translucent grey barrels and black ends, appearing consistent in color.
The leftmost pen shows a bare writing tip (or is a refill) at the bottom, whereas the other two pens clearly have black caps attached at the bottom.
The board moves continuously and smoothly from the left edge to the right edge of the frame without pausing or jamming.

parsed.reason: The leftmost pen is uncapped (showing a bare tip) while the other two are capped, violating the condition that all pens must be complete and identical.

description: One pen is missing its cap while the others are capped.
